lesson_title: Municipal Tariffs and Rising Block Systems: the Staircase on Your Bill
hook_text: 380 units of electricity. One family pays R948, the calculator says R988. The R40 gap is a staircase.
clip_script: Prepaid electricity is priced like a staircase. Your first 100 units this month stand on the cheap step — R2,20 each, that's R220. Units 101 and up climb to the next step — R2,60 each. Our household used 380 units: 100 on the bottom step, 280 on the second. R220 plus R728 — R948. Now watch the mistake half the country makes: 380 lands in block two, so multiply everything by R2,60? That's R988 — forty rand wrong, because climbing higher never re-prices the cheap steps below you. Water works the same, except the bottom step is FREE — your first six thousand litres cost nothing. But a leaking toilet? That water sits on the TOP step, R26,40 a kilolitre plus VAT — the most expensive water in your house. And when someone offers you a flat-rate deal with a monthly fee, don't guess. Calculate both at YOUR usage. Small users win on the staircase; heavy users win on the flat rate. The crossing point is break-even. Know your steps, and the bill stops being a mystery.
visual_style: A staircase of glowing blocks rising across the screen, units stacking onto each step with prices stamped on the risers; a leaking toilet dripping coins onto the top step; two cost lines crossing at a break-even point drawn in chalk.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who reads the tariff table before loading the voucher.
pacing: Brisk up the staircase, a hard stop on the R988 mistake, slow and pointed on the free water and the break-even crossing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never overpay a municipal bill again.
